Inputs are finite CARE or DARE data from [[def-standard-continuous-and-discrete-riccati-equations]], finite Schur or QZ sweep budgets, an adjacent-swap budget $K$, a scalar/evaluator work budget $W$, a positive local separation threshold $\eta$, and the exact arithmetic controller or bounded outward evaluator for [[alg-finite-budget-stable-block-reordering-for-schur-and-qz]]. For CARE form $H=\begin{bmatrix}A&-G\\-Q&-A^*\end{bmatrix}$; for DARE form $N=\begin{bmatrix}A&0\\-Q&I\end{bmatrix}$ and $M=\begin{bmatrix}I&G\\0&A^*\end{bmatrix}$. The procedure never forms $A^{-1}$ and does not require a separately supplied ordered basis.

1. For CARE, run [[alg-finite-budget-francis-schur-reduction]] on $H$. For DARE, run [[alg-finite-budget-qz-iteration-with-deflation-and-residual]] on $(N,M)$. Propagate any budget, range, invariant-pattern, or pencil-regularity failure as an explicit inconclusive status. The returned residuals and factor backward-error certificates are those specified by the corresponding supplier items; they are not interpreted as structure-preserving perturbations.
2. On a successful reduction, invoke [[alg-finite-budget-stable-block-reordering-for-schur-and-qz]] with the CARE strict-left-half-plane selector or DARE strict-unit-disk selector and required selected dimension $n$. Propagate every non-ordered result as its explicit status, including boundary-spectrum, separation-inconclusive, swap-separation-inconclusive, arithmetic-inconclusive, range-failure, swap-budget-exhausted, and work-budget-exhausted. The source algorithm's exact product factors and [F6] certify ordering of the represented computed form and preserve the original unstructured reduction residual. For CARE take the first $n$ columns of the updated Schur factor; for DARE take the first $n$ columns of the updated **right** QZ factor, never the left factor. If the relevant exact factor or residual certificate is unavailable, keep the corresponding diagnostic inconclusive.
3. Write the ordered stable basis as $U=\begin{bmatrix}U_1\\U_2\end{bmatrix}$. Estimate $\|U_1^{-1}\|_2$ using the supplied verified linear-residual certificate; if invertibility or a finite bound cannot be certified, return graph-block-inconclusive.
4. Solve $X_0U_1=U_2$ by a finite verified linear solve; do not form an explicit inverse. Set $\widehat X=(X_0+X_0^*)/2$. Compute and report the actual Riccati residual, Hermitian symmetry defect, the DARE matrix $R+B^*\widehat X B$ when applicable, the graph-block bound, and the actual closed-loop spectral certificate. Any failed positivity or stability check returns candidate-rejected; unavailable certificates return inconclusive. No residual by itself certifies the stabilizing branch or a nearby positive $Q,R$.

This is the finite candidate-extraction stage for the ordered Schur/QZ solvers. Its ordering prerequisite is the finite adjacent-block routine and correctness theorem cited above; a successful order applies to the represented computed form, with the separately stated diagnostics still required for Riccati acceptance.

Input a real or complex square matrix $A\in\mathbb F^{n\times n}$ with $n\ge1$, a finite nonnegative deflation tolerance $\tau$, a nonnegative integer sweep budget $N$, a positive integer stagnation period $h$, a finite family of exceptional-shift tables $T_{a,b}$ indexed by original contiguous index intervals $[a,b]\subseteq[1,n]$ with $a<b$, optional exact rational/dyadic encodings of its stored real values, optionally a terminating exact evaluator of [[def-exact-real-2x2-discriminant-sign-predicate]], and optionally a terminating outward evaluator for nonnegative expressions and Frobenius norms. The outward evaluator's `upadd`, `upmul`, and `upsqrt` calls return finite nonnegative represented upper bounds for the exact sum, product, and square root, while `upnormF(X)` returns a finite represented upper bound for $\|X\|_F$; any call may instead return `unavailable`. In the declared scalar-cost model, each `upadd`, `upmul`, and `upsqrt` call has unit cost and `upnormF(X)` makes one pass over the entries of $X$ with a fixed number of such calls per real component. The evaluator acts only on certificate bookkeeping. A formation `breakdown` is propagated with the operation index and partial factors. Every scalar operation in the main procedure is evaluated in the operationwise model of [[def-operationwise-real-complex-floating-point-model-with-sqrt-and-fma]]. Any invalid, overflow, or underflow operation in the main procedure returns range-failure with the operation index and partial factors.

Each complex table entry is a finite represented scalar $\mu\in\mathbb C$; each real table entry is a pair of finite represented real coefficients $(s,t)$ for $z^2-sz+t$. Each table is an ordered finite list, possibly empty; an omitted interval has the empty list. These descriptors use the field of $A$. Tables support direct indexed lookup by interval and cursor; unused entries are not scanned. All interval-state updates use a single ordered pass over the current partition. Counters and table indices are exact integers. Maintain state $(c_{a,b},q_{a,b})$, initially $(0,0)$, for each current maximal diagonal interval separated by exact zero subdiagonals: $c$ counts completed ordinary block sweeps since the last reset and $q$ counts exceptional descriptors already consumed. After a split, discard the parent state and initialize every new child interval to $(0,0)$, using its own table. An unchanged interval retains its state. Completed one-by-one blocks, and real two-by-two blocks with verified negative discriminant, require no shift.

Start with $H=A$ and the empty factor product $Q=I$. Set the completed global sweep count to $k=0$ after initialization. Before attempting any sweep, and after every completed sweep, perform steps 2 and 5, in that order. If neither returns, snapshot the remaining active intervals in increasing left endpoint, and perform steps 3 and 4 once for each snapshotted interval in that order. No deflation scan or repartition occurs during this pass. After all its intervals finish, increment $k$ by one and repeat the scan and stopping test. All intervals in a pass use their current diagonal block when reached; previously applied similarities on disjoint blocks do not reschedule a block.

Before every real or complex formation in steps 1 and 4, test the target vector componentwise for exact zero, including an external initial polynomial vector. If it is zero, mark the stage `identity`, copy all affected matrix entries unchanged, skip formation and both left and right updates, append the embedded identity $P_j=I$ to the product representation, and record $E_j=0$ and arithmetic coefficient $\alpha_j=\bar\alpha_j=0$. Do not evaluate $P(v)$ or a stored-vector norm in this branch. For a matrix target its column is already zero, so its target zero writes change nothing; for an external vector no matrix column is overwritten. Continue with the invariant checks, sweep counters and stopping tests specified below. Record and process every deflation write separately exactly as specified below; this branch does not discard a deflation perturbation. These identity instructions take precedence over the formation/update instructions in steps 1 and 4.

For each nonidentity stored reflector with active indices $S=(s_1,\ldots,s_m)$, nonzero vector $v\in\mathbb F^m$, and real computed coefficient $\widehat\tau$, the real or complex formation routine first performs the stated finite left application. Then perform the right application in this fixed order: for each matrix row $i=1,\ldots,n$, compute $d_i=\operatorname{fl}(\sum_{a=1}^m H^L_{i,s_a}v_a)$ by left-to-right rounded products and additions; for $a=1,\ldots,m$, compute $c_a=\operatorname{fl}(\widehat\tau\overline{v_a})$, $g_{ia}=\operatorname{fl}(d_ic_a)$, and $H^R_{i,s_a}=\operatorname{fl}(H^L_{i,s_a}-g_{ia})$. Each complex product uses the six real operations of the arithmetic model. The exact factor appended to $Q$ is $P(v)=I-2vv^*/(v^*v)$; the computed right update uses $\widehat\tau$ as displayed and is not asserted equal to multiplication by $P(v)$. For a matrix-target column, the formation routine's explicit zero writes are retained. In the initial polynomial-vector step there is no matrix-target column: use the entire active row panel for the left update and then apply the right update to the active columns. Record deflation writes separately, including a pure deflation with no following reflector as an identity-transform stage; a local error certificate must account for all other rounding and target-column writes.

1. Reduce $A$ to upper Hessenberg form with Householder similarities. For $k=1,\ldots,\max(n-2,0)$ in increasing order, use active indices $S=\{k+1,\ldots,n\}$, target $x=H_{S,k}$, and trailing left panel $B=H_{S,\{k+1,\ldots,n\}}$ with columns in increasing order. In the real branch use [[alg-scaled-householder-reflector-formation-and-application]] for the finite left application and overwrite; in the complex branch use [[alg-complex-scaled-householder-reflector-step]]. Complete each similarity by the right application above on columns $S$. After the entire initialization loop, including when it is empty, check the resulting matrix's exact upper-Hessenberg zero pattern; on failure return bulge-chase-invariant-failure with the partial factors. Store the exact unitary reflector factors as a product representation $Q_0$.
2. In increasing global row index $i=2,\ldots,n$, test each nonzero first-subdiagonal entry by
   $$|h_{i,i-1}|\le\tau\bigl(|h_{i-1,i-1}|+|h_{i,i}|\bigr).$$
   For a complex entry $z=a+ib$, evaluate $|z|$ by $s=\max(|a|,|b|)$ and $s\sqrt{(a/s)^2+(b/s)^2}$ when $z\ne0$, with divisions, squares, sum, square root and final scaling rounded in the stated order; use $|0|=0$. Return range-failure if this evaluation fails. Compute the diagonal-magnitude sum first, then multiply by $\tau$ in the operationwise model; compare the resulting finite values exactly. When the test holds, set that entry to zero and record its original value as a deflation perturbation. After the scan, form the maximal intervals separated by exact zero subdiagonals and update interval states by the rule above. The equality case deflates. Do not use the Hermitian-tridiagonal Wilkinson shift rule for a general Hessenberg matrix.
3. For the current snapshotted interval $[a,b]$, let $L=H_{a:b,a:b}$ and $\ell=b-a+1$. If $c_{a,b}=h$, read entry $q_{a,b}+1$ of $T_{a,b}$. If absent, return stagnation-exhausted before this block's chase. Otherwise consume it by incrementing $q_{a,b}$ once and use its complex scalar shift or real coefficient pair. After this exceptional block sweep completes, set $c_{a,b}=0$. If $c_{a,b}<h$, use the ordinary shift: in the complex branch $\mu=L_{\ell,\ell}$; in the real branch, for the trailing block $\begin{pmatrix}a'&b'\\c'&d'\end{pmatrix}$, compute $s=\operatorname{fl}(a'+d')$ then $t=\operatorname{fl}(\operatorname{fl}(a'd')-\operatorname{fl}(b'c'))$ in that order. Return range-failure on a failed operation. After this ordinary block sweep completes, increment $c_{a,b}$ by one. A split at the next scan resets each new child as specified above; unchanged intervals retain these updated states.
4. On the diagonal block $L$ selected in step 3, apply the index pattern of [[alg-exact-francis-hessenberg-qr-step]], with its dimension $\ell$ and local indices $1,\ldots,\ell$. In the vector formulas in this step, $H$ means that current diagonal block. Translate every local index $i$ to global index $a+i-1$; embed each factor in the full $n\times n$ identity. The left panel extends through global column $n$, and the right application runs through all global rows, so upper off-diagonal blocks are updated as well. For the initial single-shift vector compute $x_1=\operatorname{fl}(h_{11}-\mu)$ and $x_i=h_{i1}$ for $i>1$. For the initial real double-shift vector, compute $u=He_1$, then $w=Hu$ by left-to-right rounded matrix-vector products, then $x=\operatorname{fl}(\operatorname{fl}(w-su)+te_1)$ componentwise. Compute only the first $r+1$ components from the Hessenberg support pattern; on range failure return the operation index and partial factors. For a chase at local column $j$, use the globally translated active indices $S=I_j$, the corresponding global target column $a+j-1$, and the trailing left panel through global columns $a+j,\ldots,n$ in increasing order. Call the real or complex formation routine, write the target tail zeros exactly, complete the two-sided update by the right-kernel order above on columns $S$, and append the exact reflector representation to $Q$. In the initial polynomial-vector step there is no matrix-target column; use the full active row panel for the left update and then apply the right update to its active columns. After the block chase, perform the following exact upper-Hessenberg zero-pattern check, including when all its stages were identities. For $i=1,\ldots,n$ in increasing order, if $a\le i\le b$, test $h_{ij}=0$ for $j=1,\ldots,i-2$ in increasing order; otherwise test $h_{ij}=0$ for $j=a,\ldots,\min(b,i-2)$ in increasing order. Skip every empty index range. On the first nonzero tested entry return bulge-chase-invariant-failure with the partial matrix and factors. These are precisely the below-first-subdiagonal positions whose row or column belongs to $[a,b]$. Enumerate only these ranges; do not scan all $n^2$ positions and filter them. The unchanged complementary positions retain the zero values established by initialization or the previous accepted check. Deflation writes affect only the first subdiagonal and do not change those positions. Use [[lem-two-sided-scaled-householder-similarity-error]] to store the proved two-sided coefficient $\alpha_{m_j}=a_{m_j}+b_{m_j}+a_{m_j}b_{m_j}$, with $a$ the target-overwrite coefficient or separate-block coefficient as actually used and $b$ the right separate-block coefficient. This gives $\|E_j\|_F\le\alpha_{m_j}\|\widehat H_{j-1}\|_F$ when its $m_ju<1$ and range hypotheses hold. Apply the same certificate to every Hessenberg-initialization similarity. If any step lacks that certificate, retain the residual diagnostic and set the backward-error-certificate status to inconclusive.
5. Inspect maximal intervals in increasing left endpoint. A size-one interval is completed. A complex interval of size at least two, or a real interval of size at least three, is active. For each real size-two interval determine its exact discriminant sign as below: a negative sign completes that interval, while zero or a positive sign leaves it active. Stop with Schur-computed when all intervals are completed. Use the supplied evaluator, or the finite integer recipe in [[lem-exact-rational-two-by-two-discriminant-sign]] when exact rational/dyadic encodings are available, for each real block's $\operatorname{discSign}$ as defined in [[def-exact-real-2x2-discriminant-sign-predicate]]. If no exact sign is available, return schur-type-undecided and do not claim Schur-computed. If any active interval remains and $k=N$, return budget-exhausted; in particular, with $N=0$ return Schur-computed only when the initialized matrix already has the target block structure. Return the partial matrix and factors on every failure or nonconvergence status.

For certificate bookkeeping, start before Hessenberg initialization with $\rho_0=\operatorname{upnormF}(A)$ and $C_0=0$. If the evaluator is absent or this call is unavailable, mark the backward-error certificate inconclusive. Process each local similarity update and each deflation-only write as a separate finite stage $j$. For a local similarity, take the actual coefficient $\alpha_j=a_{m_j}+b_{m_j}+a_{m_j}b_{m_j}$ from [[lem-two-sided-scaled-householder-similarity-error]] and compute $\bar\alpha_j=\operatorname{upadd}(\operatorname{upadd}(a_{m_j},b_{m_j}),\operatorname{upmul}(a_{m_j},b_{m_j}))\ge\alpha_j$; for an identity update put $\bar\alpha_j=0$. A recorded deflation entry stores its old value, while its additive matrix $D_j$ has entry equal to zero minus that old value at the written position. For a deflation-only stage use $P_j=I$, $E_j=0$, $\bar\alpha_j=0$, and obtain $\bar\beta_j\ge\|D_j\|_F$ by calling `upnormF` on the one-entry list containing the signed recorded value, whose Frobenius norm equals $\|D_j\|_F$; do not form or scan a dense matrix $D_j$; for a similarity stage set $\bar\beta_j=0$. With the outward evaluator compute

$$g_j=\operatorname{upadd}(\operatorname{upmul}(\bar\alpha_j,\rho_{j-1}),\bar\beta_j),\qquad \rho_j=\operatorname{upadd}(\rho_{j-1},g_j),\qquad C_j=\operatorname{upadd}(C_{j-1},g_j).$$

If any local coefficient certificate or evaluator call is unavailable, keep the residual diagnostic and mark the backward-error-certificate status `inconclusive`; this ancillary failure does not change the main algorithm status. Otherwise return $C_J$ as the accumulated backward-error upper bound and mark that status `certified`. The number of recurrence calls is finite: one initialization norm, a fixed number of scalar upper-bound calls per similarity stage, and one norm call per deflation-only stage.

Let $\widehat T$ be the final returned matrix. The output includes the product representation $Q$, residual matrix $R=Q^*AQ-\widehat T$ and its Frobenius norm as diagnostics, the exact orthogonality bound $0$ for that reflector product, the recorded deflation entries, and either the accumulated backward-error bound when all local certificates exist or certificate status inconclusive. Bound expressions and any claimed upper bounds are evaluated exactly or with rigorous outward allowances; uncorrected rounded residual norms are diagnostics only. A rounded dense matrix formed from $Q$ has its own orthogonality residual and is not asserted exactly unitary. The residual diagnostic does not itself give a forward eigenvalue bound. The procedure asserts no unconditional convergence of any shift schedule.

Input a regular pencil $(A,B)$ with $A,B\in\mathbb C^{n\times n}$,
$n\ge1$, a nonnegative integer sweep budget $N$, and a finite stored real tolerance
$\tau\ge0$. Real input data are embedded in $\mathbb C$. Scalar updates of the
stored matrices use the operationwise model of
[[def-operationwise-real-complex-floating-point-model-with-sqrt-and-fma]].
Use zero-based matrix indices throughout. Each active block $[a:b]$ includes
both endpoints; its relative coordinate $0$ is global index $a$.
Use the canonical stored Givens generator and application order of
[[alg-scaled-complex-householder-and-givens-updates]], with the common-pair
orientations and explicit coefficients $v,h,\eta$ of
[[lem-qz-two-sided-local-computed-update-bound]]. Generate each rotation ONCE
and apply its same stored coefficients to BOTH matrices. Retain the exact
normalized unitary representatives as product records, never as purported
stored dense unitary matrices. Left rotations annihilate a column's second
entry; right rotations annihilating a row's first entry use the coordinate
reversal/adjoint construction of that lemma. After each genuine matrix target
application write only its intended target to exact zero and include that
write in the local coefficient $\eta$. An external-vector application has
coefficient $v$ and no matrix-target overwrite. Local roundoff certification
requires $0<u<1$; otherwise retain diagnostics with `certificate-inconclusive`. Record each elementary
rotation separately. If the source cannot produce its admissible factor,
return `range-failure` or `certificate-inconclusive` with diagnostics.

1. Execute the finite index loops of
[[alg-generalized-hessenberg-triangular-reduction]] with these COMPUTED common
rotations: triangularize $B$ with left targets $B_{i,j}$; then reduce $A$ with
left targets $A_{i,j}$ followed by right targets $B_{i,i-1}$. Every application
updates both whole arrays. The exact initializer and
[[prop-generalized-hessenberg-triangular-reduction-preserves-form-and-equivalence]]
supply the index schedule and support induction, not exact rounded
reconstruction. Retain each local factor and residual defined against its
exact representative. Include structural target writes in that local
arithmetic residual. Record all OTHER explicit zero writes separately: their
post-action perturbations are pulled back by the local factor adjoints before
entering the pre-action $D_j^A,D_j^B$ ledger. A pure tolerance write is an
identity-factor stage. Never count a structural write twice.

Initialize the sweep counter to zero. Process active blocks in increasing first
index, splitting them at exact zero subdiagonals of $H$. In each deflation
pass execute step 2, then repeat step 3 for the smallest available non-isolated
zero diagonal of $T$ until none remains or a status exits. Then run step 5; if
it returns a status, stop. Otherwise, if the sweep counter equals $N$, return
`budget-exhausted`. If not, increment the counter, execute step 4 on all
remaining active blocks, and repeat the deflation pass. In particular $N=0$
permits initialization/deflation but no step-4 sweep.

2. On each active block $H_{a:b,a:b},T_{a:b,a:b}$, apply the following deflation
tests before a sweep. For $i=a,\ldots,b-1$, set $H_{i+1,i}$ to zero when
$$|H_{i+1,i}|\le\tau\bigl(|H_{i,i}|+|H_{i+1,i+1}|\bigr),$$
and record the negative of its old value at that position in $D^A$, with
all other entries zero. For $k=a,\ldots,b$, set $T_{k,k}$ to zero when
$$|T_{k,k}|\le\tau\bigl(|T_{k-1,k}|+|T_{k,k+1}|\bigr),$$
using zero for a missing boundary term outside the active block, and record the
negative of the old value at that position in $D^B$, with all other entries zero.
Treat each write as a separate identity-factor stage, so the new matrix is
the old matrix plus its recorded perturbation.
Evaluate each displayed modulus by the canonical rounded scaled two-component
norm; evaluate its additions and tolerance product with the declared rounded
real operations, then compare the stored finite values exactly. Excluded
operations return `range-failure`. The tests mean these rounded comparisons,
not an assertion about exact moduli at the threshold. Save the actual old
entries, so their deflation perturbations remain exact regardless of the test.
A one-by-one diagonal pair at $k$ is isolated when $H_{k,k-1}=0$ and
$H_{k+1,k}=0$, omitting a boundary entry when $k=a$ or $k=b$. If it has
$T_{k,k}=0$ and $H_{k,k}\ne0$, report an infinite candidate for the computed pencil and deflate it
from the active block. If the isolated diagonal pair is $(0,0)$, return
`singular-pencil-suspected` without assigning an eigenvalue.

3. To move a non-isolated zero $T_{k,k}$ to the top of its active block, for
$j=k-1,k-2,\ldots,a$ generate a right factor from the row pair
$(T_{j,j},T_{j,j+1})$ and apply it to columns $j,j+1$, setting $T_{j,j}$ to
zero. Then, when $j+2\le b$, generate a left factor from
$(H_{j+1,j},H_{j+2,j})$ and apply it to rows $j+1,j+2$, setting the resulting
bulge $H_{j+2,j}$ to zero. Finally, when $a<b$, generate a left factor from
$(H_{a,a},H_{a+1,a})$ and apply it to rows $a,a+1$, setting $H_{a+1,a}$ to
zero. Record all rounded update residuals and target writes. If this isolates
$(H_{a,a},T_{a,a})=(h,0)$ with $h\ne0$, report the infinite candidate and
remove the first row/column from the active block.
If the isolated pair is $(0,0)$, return `singular-pencil-suspected`; if isolation
fails, return `certificate-inconclusive`. Each successful isolation removes
one index, so at most $n$ such removals occur.

4. For each remaining active block with more than one row in the current
sweep, choose the homogeneous shift $[\alpha:\beta]=[H_{b,b}:T_{b,b}]$ if this pair is nonzero and
$T_{b,b}\ne0$; if $T_{b,b}=0$, use $[0:1]$. Write
$\widehat H=H_{a:b,a:b}$ and $\widehat T=T_{a:b,a:b}$, with relative indices
$0,\ldots,b-a$, and form
$$x=(\beta\widehat H-\alpha\widehat T)e_0.$$
Compute $x_0,x_1$ using the declared rounded complex products/subtractions and
generate a left factor from $(x_0,x_1)$. Apply it to relative rows $0,1$ of
both matrices without a matrix-target overwrite. Its rounding changes the
selected factor, not its application certificate. Generate a right factor
from the row pair $(\widehat T_{1,0},\widehat T_{1,1})$ and apply it to relative
columns $0,1$, setting $\widehat T_{1,0}$ to zero. For relative
$j=1,\ldots,b-a-1$, generate a left factor from
$(\widehat H_{j,j-1},\widehat H_{j+1,j-1})$ and apply it to rows $j,j+1$,
setting the current Hessenberg bulge $\widehat H_{j+1,j-1}$ to zero; then
generate a right factor from $(\widehat T_{j+1,j},\widehat T_{j+1,j+1})$ and
apply it to columns $j,j+1$, setting $\widehat T_{j+1,j}$ to zero. Update and
retain the products $Q,Z$; record every local residual including its
structural target write. Apply the embedded transformations to the entire
pair, retaining the transformed off-block data. All divisions by a generalized
eigenvalue ratio are avoided.

5. After each infinite isolation and before every successful return, scan all
isolated diagonal pairs. Any $(0,0)$ pair returns `singular-pencil-suspected`
without an eigenvalue. Stop with `qz-computed` only when $H$ is upper triangular
and every diagonal pair is nonzero. Otherwise stop after $N$ sweeps with
`budget-exhausted`. Range failures return `range-failure` with partial factors;
unavailable local certificates return `certificate-inconclusive`. Neither a
rounded diagnostic nor a tolerance-induced infinite candidate asserts an exact
infinite eigenvalue of the original pencil.

For local-accumulation bounds use $\ell_j=\eta$ for matrix-target actions and
$\ell_j=v$ for external-vector/raw actions, plus the separately saved actual
tolerance perturbations. For an independent residual certificate execute the
factor-action/column procedure of
[[lem-qz-two-sided-local-computed-update-bound]]: use stored raw kernels without
zero overwrites, propagate their $v$ allowances, use
[[lem-rounded-linear-and-normal-residual-certificates]] only on STORED matvec
inputs, and include the final subtraction allowance. Exact normalized factor
entries are not silently treated as stored inputs. Evaluate each certificate
using the finite exact real-controller expression trees/loops in the local
lemma and component absolute sums as norm upper bounds. Controller operations
are separate from rounded update arithmetic; for rational/binary stored data
and rational $u$ this is exact rational computation. No opaque certification
oracle is used. Failure of this residual route's dimension/range hypotheses
makes that route inconclusive and does not invalidate a valid independent
local-accumulation bound. Always retain available diagnostics.

The output is $(Q,S,T,Z,\text{status})$, where $S$ is the current $H$ and $T$
is the current second matrix, the exact factor products when available, the raw
residuals $R_A=Q^*AZ-S$ and $R_B=Q^*BZ-T$, and the recorded local arithmetic
and deflation perturbations. The procedure asserts no
unconditional convergence or small-roundoff bound.

Let $F\in\{\mathbb R,\mathbb C\}$, $m,n\ge1$, $A\in F^{m\times m}$, $B\in F^{n\times n}$ and $C\in F^{m\times n}$. Inputs also include a pivot threshold $\tau\ge0$, Schur controls for each matrix, a fixed constant $c_0>0$, and nonnegative integer sweep budgets $N_A,N_B$ satisfying $N_A\le c_0m$, $N_B\le c_0n$. The local transforms, certificate checks and block substitution use exact scalar arithmetic and comparisons. The delegated Schur calls retain their specified rounded arithmetic, admissible input representations, range conditions and statuses; their returned factors remain candidates until the exact checks below succeed.

The default real-block sign controller is the fixed exact real-arithmetic expression tree $s=(a-d)^2+4bc$, followed by its sign comparisons, for [[def-exact-real-2x2-discriminant-sign-predicate]]. This uses five exact arithmetic operations and at most two sign comparisons in the declared exact local arithmetic model. For rational/dyadic encoded stored values, [[lem-exact-rational-two-by-two-discriminant-sign]] gives the finite exact integer realization; a fixed-format decoder, when used, is included in the control cost. These exact controller operations are separate from the rounded Schur matrix updates. No bit-complexity bound for integer/rational arithmetic is claimed.

Choose either bounded-controller mode, the default, or arbitrary-terminating-controller mode. In bounded mode supply a nonnegative integer per-call budget $K$. Custom sign or decoding routines are finite instruction programs over exact scalar real/integer arithmetic, comparisons, register operations and branches; no opaque callback is a unit instruction. The interpreter charges one unit per executed instruction, including decoding, the built-in tree and any custom-result verification within the same per-call $K$ budget; it checks instruction/operation validity when encountered and returns undecided on exhaustion or invalid execution. An undecided sign is propagated as the Schur type-undecided status and then outer `schur-failure`. The fixed built-in sign tree or integer recipe has a fixed finite instruction count independent of matrix dimension. Any custom reported sign must agree with the built-in exact discriminant tree before acceptance. In arbitrary-terminating mode custom programs must terminate on every supplied input; record their total executed controller work as $C_{\rm aux}$. This richer mode retains finite termination but has the additional work in its cost bound. In the cubic-cost branch $K$ and representation-control instruction costs are fixed independently of matrix dimension. Programs are executed by instruction lookup without an up-front scan of unused code.

1. Run [[alg-finite-budget-francis-schur-reduction]] on $A$ and $B$ with their supplied controls and budgets. If either call does not return `Schur-computed`, return `schur-failure` with the underlying status.

2. Treat the returned factors as candidates and verify the exact certificates. In the complex branch check $U^*U=I$, $A=UTU^*$, and upper triangularity of $T$; in the real branch check $U^TU=I$, $A=UTU^T$, and the real block upper-triangular form of [[def-real-and-complex-schur-forms]]. Perform the corresponding checks for $B=VSV^*$. If any check fails, return `schur-certificate-failure`.

3. Set $D=U^*CV$. Use the column-vectorization and Kronecker convention of [[lem-sylvester-vectorization-isometry-and-kronecker-identity]]. Partition $T$ into diagonal blocks $T_{ii}$ and $S$ into diagonal blocks $S_{jj}$ as in the exact real or complex Schur form. Traverse $j$ from left to right and, for each $j$, traverse $i$ from bottom to top. Form

$$
F_{ij}=D_{ij}-\sum_{k>i}T_{ik}Y_{kj}-\sum_{\ell<j}Y_{i\ell}S_{\ell j}.
$$

The terms on the right have already been computed in this traversal order. Define $\Phi_{ij}(Z)=T_{ii}Z+ZS_{jj}$ and its matrix representation $M_{ij}=I_{s_j}\otimes T_{ii}+S_{jj}^T\otimes I_{r_i}$ on column-vectorized blocks, where $r_i,s_j\in\{1,2\}$ are the block sizes. Let $q=r_is_j\le4$ and compute $\delta(M_{ij})$ from [[lem-small-block-determinant-separation-lower-bound]]. If $\det(M_{ij})=0$, return `singular-pivot`; if $\det(M_{ij})\ne0$ and $\delta(M_{ij})\le\tau$, return `pivot-separation-failure` because the requested pivot bound is not certified. Otherwise use the cofactor adjugate formula of [[lem-adjugate-inverse-formula-over-a-field]] to set $\operatorname{vec}(Y_{ij})=\operatorname{adj}(M_{ij})\operatorname{vec}(F_{ij})/\det(M_{ij})$ and store $Y_{ij}$. The local dimension is at most four in the real block case and one in the complex triangular case.

4. After all blocks are solved, return `success` and $X=UYV^*$, together with the exact residual $C-(AX+XB)$. No computed Schur candidate is accepted as an exact factorization unless step 2 verifies its defining equalities.

Inputs are CARE data with $Q=C^*C\succeq0$, $R\succ0$, a supplied stabilizing gain $K_0$, a finite outer budget $N$, and either exact or safeguarded-inexact solve mode. At iteration $j$, put $A_j=A-BK_j$.

In exact mode, use [[alg-bartels-stewart-sylvester-equation]] to solve
$$A_j^*X_j+X_jA_j=-(Q+K_j^*RK_j).$$
If it does not return success, stop with its status. Otherwise set $K_{j+1}=R^{-1}B^*X_j$ and continue, stopping after at most $N$ updates.

In safeguarded-inexact mode, take a proposed Hermitian approximate Lyapunov solution $\widetilde P_j$, define $\widetilde K_j=R^{-1}B^*\widetilde P_j$, and inspect the finite line-search list $\theta_\ell=2^{-\ell}$, $0\le\ell\le L$. For each trial $K_\ell=K_j+\theta_\ell(\widetilde K_j-K_j)$, let $A_\ell=A-BK_\ell$ and obtain outward-verified data: $W_\ell\succ0$, $\mu_\ell>0$ with
$$A_\ell^*W_\ell+W_\ell A_\ell\preceq-\mu_\ell I,$$
an inverse bound $\kappa_\ell\ge\|\mathcal L_{A_\ell}^{-1}\|_{F\to F}$, a residual bound $r_\ell$ for
$$\mathcal L_{A_\ell}(\widetilde P_j)+Q+K_\ell^*RK_\ell,$$
and an outward upper bound $\eta_\ell\ge\lambda_{\max}(\widetilde P_j-X_j)$. Accept the first trial satisfying $\eta_\ell+\kappa_\ell r_\ell\le0$. If none passes, return safeguard-inconclusive without changing $K_j$. The verifier uses the residual-certificate convention of [[def-verified-linear-residual-certificate-data]] and the finite-DAG enclosure guarantee of [[thm-outward-rounded-operations-are-isotone-and-dag-sound]].

After at most $N$ outer updates return the accepted gain sequence, solve residuals, cost-matrix data, and terminal status. An arbitrary approximate Lyapunov solve is never accepted without the separate stability and descent checks above.

Input $A\in F^{n\times n}$, Hermitian $G_0\succeq0$ and $H_0\succeq0$, a finite iteration budget $N$, and a finite arithmetic/range controller. Set $A_0=A$. For each $j=0,\ldots,N-1$, form
$$W_j=(I+G_jH_j)^{-1},$$
and update
$$A_{j+1}=A_jW_jA_j,\qquad G_{j+1}=G_j+A_jW_jG_jA_j^*,\qquad H_{j+1}=H_j+A_j^*H_jW_jA_j.$$
These formulas use no inverse of $A_j$. The companion recurrence-invariant proof establishes exact-arithmetic invertibility and positive-semidefinite preservation. The finite-arithmetic routine separately reports solve, range, and symmetry status.

In finite arithmetic, attempt each solve by a finite factorization routine. Return range-failure or inverse-inconclusive if the computed solve lacks its declared certificate. Preserve the raw matrices, report $\|G_j-G_j^*\|_F$ and $\|H_j-H_j^*\|_F$, and report the actual DARE residual for $H_j$ whenever its inverse is certified. Symmetrization may be used only to form a candidate and must be followed by fresh residual and positivity checks. No exact positive-semidefinite or structure-preserving backward-error claim is made from a rounded recurrence alone.

Suppose [[alg-finite-budget-qz-iteration-with-deflation-and-residual]]
returns exact unitary factor products $Q,Z$, factors $S,T$, and exact local
arithmetic and deflation residuals as specified there. If each local residual
pair has a certified bound, then the accumulated theorem
[[lem-two-sided-unitary-equivalence-errors-accumulate-for-pencil]] gives
perturbations $\Delta_A,\Delta_B$ such that
$$Q^*(A+\Delta_A)Z=S,\qquad Q^*(B+\Delta_B)Z=T,$$
with combined Frobenius error bounded by the sum of the certified local pair
errors and deflation errors. This implication is conditional: it does not
assert such a bound for an arbitrary unspecified rotation implementation. For the specified successful canonical Givens implementation, [[lem-qz-two-sided-local-computed-update-bound]] supplies $\ell_j=\eta$ for actual matrix annihilations and $\ell_j=v$ for external-vector/raw actions. With structural writes included there and only separate tolerance writes $D_{\mathrm{tol},j}$, it gives the concrete bound
$$P(\Delta_A,\Delta_B)\le\sum_j\ell_jP(A_{j-1},B_{j-1})+\sum_j P(D^A_{\mathrm{tol},j},D^B_{\mathrm{tol},j}),$$
where $P(C,D)=(\|C\|_F^2+\|D\|_F^2)^{1/2}$. Tolerance deflations need not be $O(u)$.

Independently, if the exact raw residuals are
$$R_A=Q^*AZ-S,\qquad R_B=Q^*BZ-T,$$
then the choices $\Delta_A=-Q R_A Z^*$ and $\Delta_B=-Q R_B Z^*$ satisfy the
same equations and
$$\sqrt{\|\Delta_A\|_F^2+\|\Delta_B\|_F^2} =\sqrt{\|R_A\|_F^2+\|R_B\|_F^2}.$$
Certified upper bounds on the two residual norms therefore give an
a-posteriori backward-error certificate for the pair.

Let $F\in\{\mathbb R,\mathbb C\}$, $A\in F^{n\times n}$, $B\in F^{n\times m}$, $C\in F^{p\times n}$, and $R=R^*\in F^{m\times m}$ be positive definite. Write $Q=C^*C$ and $G=BR^{-1}B^*$. The inverse $R^{-1}$ is well-defined: [[thm-cholesky-factorisation-exists-iff-hermitian-positive-definite-and-is-unique]] supplies an invertible factor $R=LL^*$, so $R^{-1}=L^{-*}L^{-1}$. Thus $v^*Gv=\|L^{-1}B^*v\|_2^2\ge0$ and $v^*Qv=\|Cv\|_2^2\ge0$. The symbol $^*$ is transpose over $\mathbb R$ and conjugate transpose over $\mathbb C$.

The **continuous algebraic Riccati equation (CARE)** is
$$A^*X+XA-XGX+Q=0.$$
Its residual is $F_c(X)=A^*X+XA-XGX+Q$, its feedback is $K_c(X)=R^{-1}B^*X$, and its closed-loop matrix is $A_c(X)=A-BK_c(X)=A-GX$.

For $X=X^*\succeq0$, $S_X:=R+B^*XB$ is positive definite because
$v^*S_Xv=v^*Rv+(Bv)^*X(Bv)>0$ for every nonzero $v$. The **discrete
algebraic Riccati equation (DARE)** is
$$X=Q+A^*XA-A^*XB(R+B^*XB)^{-1}B^*XA.$$
Its residual is $F_d(X)=Q+A^*XA-A^*XB(R+B^*XB)^{-1}B^*XA-X$. Whenever $X=X^*$, the matrix $R+B^*XB$ is positive definite if $X\succeq0$. Its feedback and closed-loop matrix are
$$K_d(X)=(R+B^*XB)^{-1}B^*XA,\qquad A_c(X)=A-BK_d(X).$$
A CARE solution is **stabilizing** when it is Hermitian and $A_c(X)$ is Hurwitz. A DARE solution is **stabilizing** when it is Hermitian, $R+B^*XB\succ0$, and $A_c(X)$ is Schur stable. No inverse of $A$ is part of either definition.

For Hermitian $X$ with $S_X$ invertible, multiplication gives
$$(I+GX)^{-1}=I-BS_X^{-1}B^*X,\qquad X(I+GX)^{-1}=X-XB S_X^{-1}B^*X.$$
In either product, the additional coefficient of $B$ is
$R^{-1}-S_X^{-1}-S_X^{-1}(B^*XB)R^{-1}=0$, because
$S_X=R+B^*XB$. Thus the DARE is equivalently
$X=Q+A^*X(I+GX)^{-1}A$, and its closed-loop matrix is
$A_c(X)=(I+GX)^{-1}A$.

The associated homogeneous symplectic pencil is
$$N=\begin{bmatrix}A&0\\-Q&I\end{bmatrix},\qquad M=\begin{bmatrix}I&G\\0&A^*\end{bmatrix},\qquad \mathcal P(\alpha,\beta)=\beta N-\alpha M.$$
The homogeneous-coordinate convention is that a finite eigenvalue
$\lambda$ is $[\alpha:\beta]=[\lambda:1]$ and $[1:0]$ denotes infinity.

Inputs are an order $d\ge0$ real or complex Schur matrix $T$, or a regular real or complex generalized Schur pair $(S,T)$, with the declared diagonal block partition. Complex Schur and QZ forms have scalar blocks; real Schur forms have scalar blocks or real $2\times2$ blocks; real generalized Schur forms have real $1\times1$ or $2\times2$ blocks. Each generalized diagonal block pair must be regular. Optional accumulated factors are exact unitary/orthogonal products; if omitted they are identity. Other inputs are a CARE selector (strict left half-plane) or DARE selector (strict unit disk), a required integer selected dimension $0\le r\le d$, nonnegative integer budgets $K$ and $W$, a positive local separation threshold $\eta$, and either an exact arithmetic controller or a bounded outward evaluator.

Use the CARE selector with an ordinary Schur form and the DARE selector with a generalized Schur form; an unmatched form-selector combination returns invalid-form.

The entries of the input arrays are treated as their exact represented real or complex values. All local transformed arrays and accumulated factors are retained exactly as finite products; a rounded dense copy is only a separately evaluated diagnostic. Before each scalar primitive or outward evaluation, return work-budget-exhausted if no units of $W$ remain; otherwise consume one unit before requesting the operation. Charge validation, label and inversion-count scans, local construction, and the final ordering scan to this same budget. For rational or dyadic arrays, the exact core uses rational arithmetic and positive square roots, with exact real-algebraic sign comparisons where needed. Exact decisions on arbitrary real inputs are an exact-real arithmetic model, not a bit-computability claim. The bounded-evaluator branch returns arithmetic-inconclusive whenever a needed zero, sign, division, or normalization remains unresolved.

1. Validate dimensions, the declared block pattern, and regularity of each generalized diagonal pair in one finite scan. For ordinary scalar blocks over either field classify $t_{ii}$ by $\operatorname{Re}t_{ii}<0$ or $>0$ for CARE; for real $2\times2$ blocks first verify negative discriminant and then classify by trace less than or greater than zero. For generalized scalar blocks over either field $[s_{ii}:t_{ii}]$, verify the pair is nonzero and classify by $|s_{ii}|<|t_{ii}|$ or $|s_{ii}|>|t_{ii}|$ for DARE; thus $t_{ii}=0$, $s_{ii}\ne0$ is complementary and represents infinity without division. For a real generalized $2\times2$ block, verify $\det(T_b)\ne0$ and that $\det(S_b-\lambda T_b)$ has negative discriminant; its conjugate roots have common squared modulus $\det(S_b)/\det(T_b)$, so classify by strict comparison of this ratio with one, cross-multiplying with the certified sign of $\det(T_b)$. Exact equality with the selected boundary returns boundary-spectrum. A bounded enclosure touching the boundary returns separation-inconclusive. Require that the selected block sizes sum to $r$, or return dimension-mismatch. Invalid patterns or singular local homogeneous pairs return invalid-form. Compute the initial inversion count once by scanning all ordered block pairs after classification.

2. Give every whole block its selected or complementary label. Locate the leftmost adjacent complementary-selected inversion. If none exists, return ordered with the current exact arrays and accumulated factors. If an inversion exists but $K$ swap attempts have already been made, return swap-budget-exhausted. Otherwise consume one attempt before starting its local construction. Never split a real conjugate pair.

3. Let $p,q\in\{1,2\}$ be the two adjacent block sizes (over $\mathbb C$, $p=q=1$), with local blocks
$$T_{JJ}=\begin{bmatrix}A&C\\0&B\end{bmatrix}$$
for ordinary Schur form, or
$$S_{JJ}=\begin{bmatrix}A&C\\0&B\end{bmatrix},\qquad T_{JJ}=\begin{bmatrix}D&F\\0&E\end{bmatrix}$$
for QZ form. With column-vectorization, form the local coefficient system
$$H=I_q\otimes A-B^T\otimes I_p,\qquad h=-\operatorname{vec}(C)$$
for ordinary Schur, with unknown $\operatorname{vec}(R)$, and
$$H=\begin{bmatrix}I_q\otimes A&-B^T\otimes I_p\\I_q\otimes D&-E^T\otimes I_p\end{bmatrix},\qquad h=-\begin{bmatrix}\operatorname{vec}(C)\\\operatorname{vec}(F)\end{bmatrix}$$
for QZ, with unknown $[\operatorname{vec}(R);\operatorname{vec}(L)]$. The transpose in $B^T$ and $E^T$ is intentional, also over $\mathbb C$. Solve $Hx=h$ and $HY=I$ by finite Gaussian elimination with complete pivoting: at each stage scan the finite remaining submatrix, choose an entry of largest certified modulus with lexicographic ties, swap rows and columns, eliminate, and back-substitute while undoing column permutations. An exact all-zero remaining submatrix returns swap-singular. An unresolved pivot or range failure returns separation-inconclusive or range-failure. Verify $Hx=h$ and $HY=I$ exactly, or verify a usable approximate-inverse certificate $\|I-YH\|_2\le\theta<1$ and still solve $Hx=h$ exactly. In the latter case it gives $\|H^{-1}\|_2\le\|Y\|_2/(1-\theta)$. In the exact-inverse branch take $\beta=\|Y\|_F$ in exact arithmetic, or an outward upper bound for that norm; in the approximate-inverse branch take an outward bound for $\|Y\|_2/(1-\theta)$. Require $\eta\beta\le1$; otherwise return swap-separation-inconclusive. Record the threshold, solves, pivot decisions and certificate.

4. For ordinary Schur form set $V=[R;I_q]$. For QZ set $V=[R;I_q]$ and $W_L=[L;I_q]$. Complete the columns of $V$, and separately $W_L$, to exact orthonormal bases by Gram–Schmidt: process the graph columns first, then $e_1,\ldots,e_{p+q}$, skipping exactly zero residuals and normalizing each nonzero residual by the positive square root of its squared norm. The graph columns are independent because their last $q$ rows form $I_q$; the coordinate scan completes a basis. An unresolved zero or normalization decision in bounded mode returns arithmetic-inconclusive.

5. Let $Z_{\rm loc}$ be the ordinary orthogonal/unitary completion; for QZ let $Z_{\rm loc}$ be the right completion and $Q_{\rm loc}$ the left completion. Propose the local transform $Z_{\rm loc}^*T Z_{\rm loc}$ in the ordinary case, or $Q_{\rm loc}^*SZ_{\rm loc}$ and $Q_{\rm loc}^*TZ_{\rm loc}$ in the QZ case. Apply it to the entire affected row and column panels, including upper off-diagonal blocks. The lower-left block is set to exact zero only by the local equations solved in step 3. For a real QZ form, factor each newly formed real $2\times2$ diagonal block as $T_b=L_bR_b$ by Gram–Schmidt on its two columns, apply the embedded $L_b^*$ to the corresponding rows of both arrays, and update $Q_{\rm loc}\leftarrow Q_{\rm loc}L_b$ with the same embedded factor; such a block is nonsingular because its roots are finite and nonreal. A size-one infinite pair requires no division by its zero second coordinate. Commit the provisional panels and factor updates only after every required local operation succeeds; otherwise return the previous committed arrays with a failed-attempt diagnostic.

6. After a committed exchange, swap the two labels and sizes and return to step 2. Ordinary accumulated factors are updated by right multiplication with $Z_{\rm loc}$; generalized accumulated factors are updated as $Q\leftarrow QQ_{\rm loc}$ and $Z\leftarrow ZZ_{\rm loc}$. The first $r$ columns of the updated factor are reported as the selected basis candidate; in QZ the right factor $Z$, not the left factor $Q$, supplies the right deflating basis.

On every exit return the current partial form, exact product factors, status, selected dimension, boundary and separation predicates, initial inversion count, attempts, accepted swaps, primitive/evaluator counts, original residual certificates, local inverse-norm certificates, and any residual transport data. Other statuses are work-budget-exhausted, arithmetic-inconclusive, range-failure, invalid-form, dimension-mismatch, boundary-spectrum, separation-inconclusive, swap-singular, swap-separation-inconclusive, and swap-budget-exhausted. ordered is distinct from any Riccati acceptance status. Reordering a computed form does not assert a structured Hamiltonian or symplectic backward-error theorem.

For an order-$d$ real or complex Schur form, or a regular generalized Schur form, run [[alg-finite-budget-stable-block-reordering-for-schur-and-qz]] with its declared selector, selected dimension $r$, swap budget $K$, primitive/evaluator budget $W$, and positive local threshold $\eta$. Every execution returns after its finite scans or an explicit budget, boundary, form, separation, arithmetic, or range status. Every committed exact swap uses orthogonal/unitary transformations, preserves the appropriate Schur form over the original field, and exchanges exactly the two adjacent block spectra; for generalized Schur form it exchanges the homogeneous roots with multiplicity, including infinity.

Let $b$ be the initial number of diagonal blocks and $I$ the number of complementary-before-selected block pairs. If the initial selected block sizes sum to $r$, all selector comparisons are strict, every local construction and certificate succeeds, every inverse-norm threshold passes, $K\ge I$, and $W$ suffices for the entire execution, including validation, label and inversion scans, all $I$ swaps, and the final ordering scan, the procedure returns ordered. The first $r$ columns of the updated ordinary Schur factor then span the selected invariant subspace of the current computed form; the first $r$ columns of the updated right QZ factor span the selected right deflating subspace of the current computed pencil. When an original reduction residual is present, this is the exact subspace of its represented nearby matrix or pencil, not automatically the original data's subspace. Each accepted swap decreases the inversion count by one and $I\le b(b-1)/2$. Boundary, small-gap, arithmetic, or budget exits do not prove that a stabilizing Riccati solution does not exist.

If the ordinary input relation is $Q_0^*AQ_0=T_0+R_0$ and the cumulative exact reordering factor is $V$, then $Q_{\rm new}=Q_0V$, $T_{\rm new}=V^*T_0V$, and the new residual is $V^*R_0V$, with unchanged Frobenius norm. If the generalized input relations are $Q_0^*AZ_0=S_0+R_A$ and $Q_0^*BZ_0=T_0+R_B$, then for cumulative left and right factors $U,V$ the new residuals are $U^*R_AV$ and $U^*R_BV$, again with unchanged Frobenius norms. Thus exact reordering preserves the original unstructured reduction certificate but creates no structured Hamiltonian or symplectic error theorem.

For $k$ local swap attempts, the scalar-core work is $O(d^2+kd)$ in the declared exact scalar/evaluator unit model: the initial structure scan costs $O(d^2)$ and each local system has order at most eight while whole-panel updates touch $O(d)$ entries. On success $k=I$, so the worst-case swap core is $O(d^3)$. Exact algebraic bit cost, evaluator implementation cost beyond the declared units, and dense evaluation of product factors are separate. From $L_0$ bounded-support input factors, directly evaluating the first $r$ columns costs $O(L_0dr+Idr)$; a dense residual multiplication, if used, has its own actual $O(d^3)$ cost.

For admitted inputs of [[alg-bartels-stewart-sylvester-equation]], the procedure terminates with a declared status, using its finite Schur controls and bounded controller programs or the stated arbitrary-terminating controller mode. Every stored local solve is unique. On `success`, the full equation $AX+XB=C$ has exactly one solution, namely the returned $X$, without an additional spectral-disjointness assumption: successful exact local pivot checks themselves imply invertibility of the full block operator. Failure or a positive threshold rejection proves neither singularity nor nonexistence unless its exact tests explicitly do so.

derivations.claim: In a Householder Hessenberg reduction, there are at most $n$ reflectors. At each stage a reflector updates a trailing block with at most $n^2$ entries using matrix-vector and rank-one operations, so the initialization costs $O(n^3)$. In a Francis or QZ bulge-chasing sweep, there are $O(n)$ rotations/reflections; each is applied to $O(n)$ entries in the active matrix and accumulated factor, hence a sweep costs $O(n^2)$. The finite budgets in [F2]–[F3] therefore give $O(n^3+sn^2)$ core work.

Dense LU factorization of $U_1$ costs $O(n^3)$; applying its factors to $n$ right-hand sides costs $O(n^3)$. The residual product $(XU_1-U_2)$ is also $O(n^3)$, yielding the candidate solve count in [F1]. In the Lyapunov branch, [F4] imposes $N_A,N_B\le c_0n$. By step 1.1, each of its two dense Schur reductions therefore costs $O(n^3)$; exact certificate checks and factor transformations are also $O(n^3)$. Triangular substitution for $n^2$ unknown entries with $O(n)$ work per entry costs $O(n^3)$, so one solve in this cubic branch costs $O(n^3)$. The fixed controller is bounded there; arbitrary-terminating-controller work is separate.

Let $d$ be the reduction order, $b$ its diagonal block count and $I$ its initial inversion count. The reordering validation scan costs $O(d^2)$. Each local system has order at most eight, and each exact factor update touches $O(d)$ panel entries, so $k$ attempts cost $O(d^2+kd)$ by [F9]. Each exact Newton-Kleinman pass has one Bartels–Stewart solve by [F5], costing $O(n^3)$ by step 2.1. Factorizing $R$ once costs $O(m^3)$. With $m$ controls, forming $B^*X$ and the gain uses $O(n^2m+m^2n)$ arithmetic including triangular solves with this pre-factored $R$; forming $K^*RK$ and $A-BK$ is bounded by the same $O(n^2m+nm^2)$ term. Summing over $J$ passes gives $O(m^3+Jn^3+J(n^2m+nm^2))$. It contains no premise that the perturbation preserves Hamiltonian or symplectic block relations, nor that it preserves positive definiteness of $Q$ or $R$. Let $F\in\{\mathbb R,\mathbb C\}$, $A\in F^{n\times n}$, $B\in F^{n\times m}$, $C\in F^{p\times n}$, and $R=R^*\in F^{m\times m}$ be positive definite. Write $Q=C^*C$ and $G=BR^{-1}B^*$. The inverse $R^{-1}$ is well-defined: [[thm-cholesky-factorisation-exists-iff-hermitian-positive-definite-and-is-unique]] supplies an invertible factor $R=LL^*$, so $R^{-1}=L^{-*}L^{-1}$. Thus $v^*Gv=\|L^{-1}B^*v\|_2^2\ge0$ and $v^*Qv=\|Cv\|_2^2\ge0$. The symbol $^*$ is transpose over $\mathbb R$ and conjugate transpose over $\mathbb C$.

The **continuous algebraic Riccati equation (CARE)** is
$$A^*X+XA-XGX+Q=0.$$
Its residual is $F_c(X)=A^*X+XA-XGX+Q$, its feedback is $K_c(X)=R^{-1}B^*X$, and its closed-loop matrix is $A_c(X)=A-BK_c(X)=A-GX$.

For $X=X^*\succeq0$, $S_X:=R+B^*XB$ is positive definite because
$v^*S_Xv=v^*Rv+(Bv)^*X(Bv)>0$ for every nonzero $v$. The **discrete
algebraic Riccati equation (DARE)** is
$$X=Q+A^*XA-A^*XB(R+B^*XB)^{-1}B^*XA.$$
Its residual is $F_d(X)=Q+A^*XA-A^*XB(R+B^*XB)^{-1}B^*XA-X$. Whenever $X=X^*$, the matrix $R+B^*XB$ is positive definite if $X\succeq0$. Its feedback and closed-loop matrix are
$$K_d(X)=(R+B^*XB)^{-1}B^*XA,\qquad A_c(X)=A-BK_d(X).$$
A CARE solution is **stabilizing** when it is Hermitian and $A_c(X)$ is Hurwitz. A DARE solution is **stabilizing** when it is Hermitian, $R+B^*XB\succ0$, and $A_c(X)$ is Schur stable. No inverse of $A$ is part of either definition.

For Hermitian $X$ with $S_X$ invertible, multiplication gives
$$(I+GX)^{-1}=I-BS_X^{-1}B^*X,\qquad X(I+GX)^{-1}=X-XB S_X^{-1}B^*X.$$
In either product, the additional coefficient of $B$ is
$R^{-1}-S_X^{-1}-S_X^{-1}(B^*XB)R^{-1}=0$, because
$S_X=R+B^*XB$. Thus the DARE is equivalently
$X=Q+A^*X(I+GX)^{-1}A$, and its closed-loop matrix is
$A_c(X)=(I+GX)^{-1}A$.

The associated homogeneous symplectic pencil is
$$N=\begin{bmatrix}A&0\\-Q&I\end{bmatrix},\qquad M=\begin{bmatrix}I&G\\0&A^*\end{bmatrix},\qquad \mathcal P(\alpha,\beta)=\beta N-\alpha M.$$
The homogeneous-coordinate convention is that a finite eigenvalue
$\lambda$ is $[\alpha:\beta]=[\lambda:1]$ and $[1:0]$ denotes infinity.

Let $F\in\{\mathbb R,\mathbb C\}$, $m,n\ge1$, $A\in F^{m\times m}$ and $B\in F^{n\times n}$. Spectra of real matrices are taken over $\mathbb C$. The map $\mathcal S_{A,B}$ of [[def-sylvester-operator-and-separation-number]] is invertible if and only if

$$
\sigma(A)\cap(-\sigma(B))=\varnothing.
$$

Equivalently, for every $C\in F^{m\times n}$, the equation $AX+XB=C$ has a unique solution if and only if this spectral condition holds. The same condition is equivalent to $\operatorname{sep}(A,-B)>0$.

Let $n\ge1$, let $\mathcal A$ be a nonempty set of matrices in $\mathbb C^{n\times n}$, and let $\mathcal b$ be a nonempty subset of $\mathbb C^n$. A **uniform residual certificate** consists of a point matrix $R\in\mathbb C^{n\times n}$, a point vector $\widehat x\in\mathbb C^n$, and numbers $q,r\ge0$ such that
$$
\|I-RA\|_2\le q,\qquad \|R(b-A\widehat x)\|_2\le r
$$
for every $A\in\mathcal A$ and $b\in\mathcal b$. Here $\|\cdot\|_2$ is the operator norm induced by the Euclidean vector norm, as in [[def-operator-norm-on-a-finite-dimensional-inner-product-space]]. The certificate is **usable** when $q<1$; in that case its reported error radius is $r/(1-q)$. The point-data case is $\mathcal A=\{A\}$ and $\mathcal b=\{b\}$.

For real intervals, complex rectangles or complex balls on which an operation
is defined, enlarging either input enclosure cannot shrink the computed
enclosure: for binary $\circ\in\{+,-,\times,\div\}$, if $X\subseteq X'$ and
$Y\subseteq Y'$, then the computed set enclosure of $X\circ Y$ is contained
in that of $X'\circ Y'$ whenever both are finite results and their domain
restrictions are preserved. The square-root enclosure is inclusion-isotone on
nonnegative intervals. Each finite ball operation in
[[def-outward-rounded-interval-and-ball-operations]] contains the exact ball
image. A `split-domain`, `entire`, `domain-error`, `overflow`, or
`inconclusive` status makes no finite claim. For a finite expression DAG
whose operation nodes all return finite enclosures, every exact node value
from every admissible input assignment belongs to its computed node
enclosure; in particular, the root enclosure contains the exact range. If any
node returns a non-finite status, no finite DAG enclosure is asserted.

Let $\mathbb F$ be $\mathbb R$ or $\mathbb C$, let $A\in M_{m\times n}(\mathbb F)$, and
let $\sigma_1\ge\sigma_2\ge\cdots\ge\sigma_r>0$ be the positive singular values of
$A$, where $r=\operatorname{rank}A$; write $\sigma_1=0$ when $r=0$.

1. **Spectral formula.** $\lVert A\rVert_2=\sigma_1$, where $\lVert\cdot\rVert_2$ is
   the operator norm of [[def-operator-norm-on-a-finite-dimensional-inner-product-space]].
2. **Frobenius formula.** $\lVert A\rVert_F=\bigl(\sigma_1^{2}+\cdots+\sigma_r^{2}\bigr)^{1/2}$.
3. **Unitary invariance.** For every unitary $U\in M_m(\mathbb F)$ and
   $V\in M_n(\mathbb F)$ (over $\mathbb F=\mathbb R$: orthogonal matrices),
   $$\lVert UAV\rVert_2=\lVert A\rVert_2,\qquad \lVert UAV\rVert_F=\lVert A\rVert_F.$$
4. **Sharp rank comparison.**
   $$\lVert A\rVert_2\;\le\;\lVert A\rVert_F\;\le\;\sqrt{r}\,\lVert A\rVert_2.$$
   The lower inequality is an equality exactly when $r\le 1$; the upper
   inequality is an equality exactly when $\sigma_1=\cdots=\sigma_r$, that is,
   when all nonzero singular values coincide. In particular
   $\lVert A\rVert_F\le\sqrt{\min(m,n)}\,\lVert A\rVert_2$.

For compatible linear maps between finite-dimensional real or complex inner
product spaces,

$$\lVert ST\rVert\le \lVert S\rVert\,\lVert T\rVert.$$

For every such linear map $T$,

$$\lVert T^*T\rVert=\lVert T\rVert^2.$$

Let $A\in F^{n\times n}$, $B\in F^{n\times m}$, $C\in F^{p\times n}$, $R=R^*\succ0$, $Q=C^*C$, and $G=BR^{-1}B^*$. Assume $(A,B)$ is continuously stabilizable and $(A,C)$ is continuously detectable, using [[def-lqr-stabilizability-and-detectability]]. Then the CARE of [[def-standard-continuous-and-discrete-riccati-equations]] has exactly one Hermitian positive-semidefinite solution $X$. Its closed-loop matrix $A_c=A-GX$ is Hurwitz, and for every initial state $x_0$ the infinite-horizon value
$$\inf_u\int_0^\infty\bigl(x(t)^*Qx(t)+u(t)^*Ru(t)\bigr)\,dt=x_0^*Xx_0$$
is attained by $u(t)=-R^{-1}B^*Xx(t)$. Controls are locally square-integrable and states are locally absolutely continuous solutions of $\dot x=Ax+Bu$. A finite value also forces the terminal term $x(T)^*Xx(T)$ to tend to zero; this transversality is proved below.

Let $A\in F^{n\times n}$ be Hurwitz and let $Q=Q^*\in F^{n\times n}$. Then the improper matrix integral

$$
X=\int_0^\infty e^{tA}Qe^{tA^*}\,dt
$$

converges and is the unique solution of $AX+XA^*+Q=0$. If $Q\succeq0$, then $X\succeq0$. If $Q\succ0$, then $X\succ0$. For $Q\succeq0$, $X\succ0$ if and only if there is no nonzero $v$ for which $e^{tA^*}v\in\ker Q^{1/2}$ for every $t\ge0$.

Let $X$ be a normed space over $\mathbb K\in\{\mathbb R,\mathbb C\}$ and assume
$X$ admits an ordered basis of finite length. Then $X$ is a Banach space in the
sense of [[def-banach-space]].

derivations.claim: For Hermitian $E$, direct expansion gives $F_c(\widehat X+E)=F_c(\widehat X)+\mathcal L(E)-EGE.$ Thus the root equation is equivalent to $E=\mathcal T(E):=-\mathcal L^{-1}F_c(\widehat X)+\mathcal L^{-1}(EGE).$

By [F5], $\|EGE\|_F\le g\|E\|_F^2$. The assumptions give $\|\mathcal T(E)\|_F\le\kappa(r+g\rho^2)\le\rho$ on the closed ball. Also $EGE-FGF=(E-F)GE+FG(E-F),$ so [F5] gives $\|\mathcal T(E)-\mathcal T(F)\|_F\le2\kappa g\rho\|E-F\|_F$ there. The Hermitian matrices form a closed finite-dimensional normed space, complete by [F9]. Iterating $\mathcal T$ from zero gives successive differences bounded by a geometric sequence of ratio $2\kappa g\rho<1$, hence a Cauchy sequence. Its limit lies in the closed ball and is a fixed point by continuity. Any two fixed points have distance at most that ratio times their distance, so they coincide.

Let $X=\widehat X+E$ be this root. Its closed loop is $A_c(X)=\widehat A_c-GE$. Expanding, $A_c(X)^*W+WA_c(X)=\widehat A_c^*W+W\widehat A_c-EGW-WGE.$ By [F6] and [A1], $\|EGW+WGE\|_2\le2\|W\|_2g\rho<\gamma$. Hence the left side is negative definite. For any eigenpair $A_c(X)v=\lambda v$, $v\ne0$, this gives $2\operatorname{Re}(\lambda)v^*Wv<0$; since $W\succ0$, $\operatorname{Re}\lambda<0$. Thus the root is stabilizing. Its CARE identity also gives $A_c(X)^*X+XA_c(X)=-(Q+XGX).$ Here $Q+XGX\succeq0$ because $Q,G\succeq0$. Since $A_c(X)$ is Hurwitz, [F8] says the unique Lyapunov solution is its positive-semidefinite integral; uniqueness from [F2] identifies that solution with $X$. Thus $X\succeq0$, and [F7] identifies it with the unique stabilizing positive-semidefinite solution.

derivations.claim: For any Hermitian $E$ with $\|E\|_F\le\rho$, [F3] and [F4] give $S(\widehat X+E)=S(\widehat X)+B^*EB\succeq(\delta_0-b^2\rho)I=\delta I.$ Thus $S(X)$ is invertible on the ball and $\|S(X)^{-1}\|_2\le\delta^{-1}$. The resolvent identity gives $\|S(X)^{-1}-S(Y)^{-1}\|_2\le b^2\delta^{-2}\|X-Y\|_F.$ Using $K(X)=S(X)^{-1}B^*XA$ and splitting the difference into the change in $X$ and the change in $S^{-1}$ yields $\|K(X)-K(Y)\|_F\le L_K\|X-Y\|_F,\qquad \|A_c(X)\|_2\le M_c,\quad \|A_c(X)-A_c(Y)\|_2\le L_c\|X-Y\|_F.$

Differentiating $S^{-1}S=I$ gives $d(S^{-1})[E]=-S^{-1}(B^*EB)S^{-1}$. Substituting this in the derivative of $F_d$ and using $K=S^{-1}B^*XA$ gives $F_d'(X)[E]=A_c(X)^*EA_c(X)-E.$ Consequently, for $D_X=F_d'(X)$ and $D_Y=F_d'(Y)$, [F4]–[F5] give $\|D_X-D_Y\|_{F\to F}\le(\|A_c(X)\|_2+\|A_c(Y)\|_2)\|A_c(X)-A_c(Y)\|_2\le L_D\|X-Y\|_F.$ Integrating the derivative along the segment from $\widehat X$ to $\widehat X+E$ gives a Taylor remainder $R(E)$ with $F_d(\widehat X+E)=F_d(\widehat X)+D(E)+R(E),\qquad \|R(E)\|_F\le L_D\|E\|_F^2/2.$

The root equation is the fixed-point equation $E=\mathcal T(E):=-D^{-1}F_d(\widehat X)-D^{-1}R(E).$ The assumptions make $\mathcal T$ a self-map of the closed ball. For $E,F$ in that ball, integrating $D_X-D$ along the segment between them gives $\|R(E)-R(F)\|_F\le L_D\rho\|E-F\|_F,$ so $\mathcal T$ has contraction factor at most $\kappa L_D\rho<1$. Iteration from zero has successive differences bounded by a geometric sequence, hence is Cauchy. The closed Hermitian ball is complete by [F8], so the sequence converges in the ball; continuity makes its limit a fixed point. The same contraction inequality makes it unique.

Let $X=\widehat X+E$ be the root. Then $\|A_c(X)-\widehat A_c\|_2\le L_c\rho=\eta$. Expanding the Stein form, $A_c(X)^*WA_c(X)-\widehat A_c^*W\widehat A_c=\widehat A_c^*W\Delta+\Delta^*W\widehat A_c+\Delta^*W\Delta,$ where $\Delta=A_c(X)-\widehat A_c$. Inputs are CARE data with $Q=C^*C\succeq0$, $R\succ0$, a supplied stabilizing gain $K_0$, a finite outer budget $N$, and either exact or safeguarded-inexact solve mode. At iteration $j$, put $A_j=A-BK_j$.

In exact mode, use [[alg-bartels-stewart-sylvester-equation]] to solve
$$A_j^*X_j+X_jA_j=-(Q+K_j^*RK_j).$$
If it does not return success, stop with its status. Otherwise set $K_{j+1}=R^{-1}B^*X_j$ and continue, stopping after at most $N$ updates.

In safeguarded-inexact mode, take a proposed Hermitian approximate Lyapunov solution $\widetilde P_j$, define $\widetilde K_j=R^{-1}B^*\widetilde P_j$, and inspect the finite line-search list $\theta_\ell=2^{-\ell}$, $0\le\ell\le L$. For each trial $K_\ell=K_j+\theta_\ell(\widetilde K_j-K_j)$, let $A_\ell=A-BK_\ell$ and obtain outward-verified data: $W_\ell\succ0$, $\mu_\ell>0$ with
$$A_\ell^*W_\ell+W_\ell A_\ell\preceq-\mu_\ell I,$$
an inverse bound $\kappa_\ell\ge\|\mathcal L_{A_\ell}^{-1}\|_{F\to F}$, a residual bound $r_\ell$ for
$$\mathcal L_{A_\ell}(\widetilde P_j)+Q+K_\ell^*RK_\ell,$$
and an outward upper bound $\eta_\ell\ge\lambda_{\max}(\widetilde P_j-X_j)$. Accept the first trial satisfying $\eta_\ell+\kappa_\ell r_\ell\le0$. If none passes, return safeguard-inconclusive without changing $K_j$. The verifier uses the residual-certificate convention of [[def-verified-linear-residual-certificate-data]] and the finite-DAG enclosure guarantee of [[thm-outward-rounded-operations-are-isotone-and-dag-sound]].

After at most $N$ outer updates return the accepted gain sequence, solve residuals, cost-matrix data, and terminal status. An arbitrary approximate Lyapunov solve is never accepted without the separate stability and descent checks above.

Let $A\in F^{n\times n}$, $B\in F^{n\times m}$, $C\in F^{p\times n}$, $R=R^*\succ0$, $Q=C^*C$, and $G=BR^{-1}B^*$. Assume $(A,B)$ is continuously stabilizable and $(A,C)$ is continuously detectable, using [[def-lqr-stabilizability-and-detectability]]. Then the CARE of [[def-standard-continuous-and-discrete-riccati-equations]] has exactly one Hermitian positive-semidefinite solution $X$. Its closed-loop matrix $A_c=A-GX$ is Hurwitz, and for every initial state $x_0$ the infinite-horizon value
$$\inf_u\int_0^\infty\bigl(x(t)^*Qx(t)+u(t)^*Ru(t)\bigr)\,dt=x_0^*Xx_0$$
is attained by $u(t)=-R^{-1}B^*Xx(t)$. Controls are locally square-integrable and states are locally absolutely continuous solutions of $\dot x=Ax+Bu$. A finite value also forces the terminal term $x(T)^*Xx(T)$ to tend to zero; this transversality is proved below.

Let $A\in F^{n\times n}$ be Hurwitz and let $Q=Q^*\in F^{n\times n}$. Then the improper matrix integral

$$
X=\int_0^\infty e^{tA}Qe^{tA^*}\,dt
$$

converges and is the unique solution of $AX+XA^*+Q=0$. If $Q\succeq0$, then $X\succeq0$. If $Q\succ0$, then $X\succ0$. For $Q\succeq0$, $X\succ0$ if and only if there is no nonzero $v$ for which $e^{tA^*}v\in\ker Q^{1/2}$ for every $t\ge0$.

Let $A\in\mathbb C^{n\times n}$ be Hurwitz, let $\alpha=-\max\{\operatorname{Re}\lambda:\lambda\in\sigma(A)\}>0$, and write $e^{tA}=\sum_{k=0}^{\infty}t^kA^k/k!$. If $A=UTU^*$ is a unitary Schur triangularization and $T=D+N$ with $D$ diagonal and $N$ strictly upper triangular, then for every $t\ge0$,

$$
\|e^{tA}\|_2\le e^{-\alpha t}\sum_{k=0}^{n-1}\frac{(t\|N\|_2)^k}{k!}.
$$

For real Hurwitz $A$, the same bound holds for its real matrix exponential, with the complex operator norm of its realification equal to the real one.

Let $F\in\{\mathbb R,\mathbb C\}$, $A\in F^{n\times n}$, $B\in F^{n\times m}$, $C\in F^{p\times n}$, and $R=R^*\in F^{m\times m}$ be positive definite. Write $Q=C^*C$ and $G=BR^{-1}B^*$. The inverse $R^{-1}$ is well-defined: [[thm-cholesky-factorisation-exists-iff-hermitian-positive-definite-and-is-unique]] supplies an invertible factor $R=LL^*$, so $R^{-1}=L^{-*}L^{-1}$. Thus $v^*Gv=\|L^{-1}B^*v\|_2^2\ge0$ and $v^*Qv=\|Cv\|_2^2\ge0$. The symbol $^*$ is transpose over $\mathbb R$ and conjugate transpose over $\mathbb C$.

The **continuous algebraic Riccati equation (CARE)** is
$$A^*X+XA-XGX+Q=0.$$
Its residual is $F_c(X)=A^*X+XA-XGX+Q$, its feedback is $K_c(X)=R^{-1}B^*X$, and its closed-loop matrix is $A_c(X)=A-BK_c(X)=A-GX$.

For $X=X^*\succeq0$, $S_X:=R+B^*XB$ is positive definite because
$v^*S_Xv=v^*Rv+(Bv)^*X(Bv)>0$ for every nonzero $v$. The **discrete
algebraic Riccati equation (DARE)** is
$$X=Q+A^*XA-A^*XB(R+B^*XB)^{-1}B^*XA.$$
Its residual is $F_d(X)=Q+A^*XA-A^*XB(R+B^*XB)^{-1}B^*XA-X$. Whenever $X=X^*$, the matrix $R+B^*XB$ is positive definite if $X\succeq0$. Its feedback and closed-loop matrix are
$$K_d(X)=(R+B^*XB)^{-1}B^*XA,\qquad A_c(X)=A-BK_d(X).$$

For Hermitian $X$ with $S_X$ invertible, multiplication gives
$$(I+GX)^{-1}=I-BS_X^{-1}B^*X,\qquad X(I+GX)^{-1}=X-XB S_X^{-1}B^*X.$$
In either product, the additional coefficient of $B$ is
$R^{-1}-S_X^{-1}-S_X^{-1}(B^*XB)R^{-1}=0$, because
$S_X=R+B^*XB$. Thus the DARE is equivalently
$X=Q+A^*X(I+GX)^{-1}A$, and its closed-loop matrix is
$A_c(X)=(I+GX)^{-1}A$.

The associated homogeneous symplectic pencil is
$$N=\begin{bmatrix}A&0\\-Q&I\end{bmatrix},\qquad M=\begin{bmatrix}I&G\\0&A^*\end{bmatrix},\qquad \mathcal P(\alpha,\beta)=\beta N-\alpha M.$$
The homogeneous-coordinate convention is that a finite eigenvalue
$\lambda$ is $[\alpha:\beta]=[\lambda:1]$ and $[1:0]$ denotes infinity.

Equality forces $K_{j+1}v=0$ and $\Delta_jv=0$, hence $K_jv=0$ and $A_jv=Av=\lambda v$, contradicting that $A_j$ is Hurwitz. Starting from $K_0$, induction proves every $A_j$ Hurwitz and every $X_j\succeq0$.

Subtracting the Lyapunov equations for $X_j$ and $X_{j+1}$ after expressing both under $A_{j+1}$ gives $A_{j+1}^*(X_j-X_{j+1})+(X_j-X_{j+1})A_{j+1}=-\Delta_j^*R\Delta_j.$ The Lyapunov integral [F3] therefore yields $X_j-X_{j+1}\succeq0$. The decreasing sequence is bounded below by zero, so each quadratic form converges. Evaluating at $e_i$, $e_i+e_j$, and $e_i+\mathrm i e_j$ shows convergence of every matrix entry to a Hermitian limit $X_\infty\succeq0$. Since $K_{j+1}=R^{-1}B^*X_j$, the gains also converge. Passing to the limit in the policy Lyapunov equation gives the CARE for $X_\infty$; [F2] identifies this positive-semidefinite root as $X_*$.

Let $E_j=X_j-X_*$ and $A_*=A-BR^{-1}B^*X_*$. Put $D_j=K_{j+1}-K_*=R^{-1}B^*E_j$. Subtract the CARE identity at $X_*$ from the policy Lyapunov equation under $A_{j+1}$ to obtain $A_{j+1}^*E_{j+1}+E_{j+1}A_{j+1}=-D_j^*RD_j.$ By [F2], $A_*$ is Hurwitz. Choose $W=\int_0^\infty e^{tA_*^*}Ie^{tA_*}\,dt\succ0$ using [F3], so $A_*^*W+WA_*=-I$. Since $A_{j+1}\to A_*$, for all large $j$ one has $A_{j+1}^*W+WA_{j+1}\preceq-\tfrac12I$. Along $\dot x=A_{j+1}x$, differentiation gives $\frac{d}{dt}(x^*Wx)\le-\frac12\|x\|_2^2\le-\frac{1}{2\|W\|_2}x^*Wx.$ Consequently $\|e^{tA_{j+1}}\|_2\le M e^{-\alpha t}$ with $M=(\|W\|_2/\lambda_{\min}(W))^{1/2}$ and $\alpha=1/(4\|W\|_2)$, uniformly for all sufficiently large $j$. Applying the Lyapunov integral to the error equation yields $\|E_{j+1}\|_F\le\left(\int_0^\infty M^2e^{-2\alpha t}\,dt\right)\|R\|_2\|R^{-1}B^*\|_2^2\|E_j\|_F^2.$ The integral is finite and supplies the stated local quadratic constant.
